item.title: Managing Users in Active Directory
item.description: Why Learn User Management in Active Directory Managing user accounts is one of the most essential responsibilities of a Windows Server administrator. This guide walks through: Creating a user First-time login on Windows 10 Resetting passwords Disabling and enabling accounts Deleting users and seeing the authentication outcome Each step includes screenshots for clear documentation and learning. Note: This is a detailed post with many screenshots and multiple sections. To navigate quickly, use your browser’s search function (Ctrl + F or Cmd + F) and look for keywords such as create, reset, enable, disable, or delete depending on the task you want to review.

item.title: Setting Up Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) on Windows Server
item.description: Why Set Up Active Directory in a Lab Setting up Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) in a virtualized environment is one of the best ways to learn Windows Server administration. This lab allows you to: Practice domain creation and management. Understand authentication and centralized user administration. Connect a Windows 10 client to a domain. Prepare for more advanced topics like Group Policy, DNS, and user management. This setup uses a Windows Server VM as the Domain Controller (DC) and a Windows 10 VM as the domain client.

item.title: Installing Windows Server on VirtualBox for a Lab
item.description: Why Install Windows Server on a Virtual Machine Installing Windows Server on VirtualBox allows you to: Experiment with server administration in a safe environment. Test networking and domain features without affecting your main PC. Prepare a base server VM for future labs, such as Active Directory setups. Step 1 — Download and Install VirtualBox Go to the VirtualBox website and download the installer for Windows Hosts. Install VirtualBox on your PC following the installer prompts.
